title: Cross-team deployment simulation notes for LLM experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for simulating cross-functional deployment choreography for LLM-backed features. The doc captures small-batch simulation scenarios, signal mappings, escalation playpaths, and synthetic traffic recipes we can run before a real canary or A/B exposure. Goal: reduce surprise during live rollouts and validate our canary-to-fallback transitions end-to-end across product, infra, SRE, and trust/safety.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: product owners, rollout stewards, SRE, infra, research applied-ML, trust & safety, release engineering.
- Scope: pre-launch simulation runs (lab), pre-canary checklists, decision heuristics for progressive enablement and automated rollback, and comms templates for a simulated incident.

Key simulation scenarios to cover (priority order):
1) Latency amplification under bursty prompt patterns
   - Synthetic profile: 20% long-context prompts (>2k tokens), 80% short queries.
   - Failure modes to observe: queue growth, KV cache thrash, degraded tail p95->p99 spikes.
   - Expected thresholds: p95 latency > 800ms for more than 3 minutes -> trigger infra alarm.

2) Quality regression on rerank/rerank+generation mix
   - Synthetic profile: 60% reranker calls (fast), 40% generation.
   - Injected regression: swapped model variant with slightly higher hallucination rate.
   - Signal mapping: increase in negative-feedback events, manual flags from human review, drop in NPS/accept rate.

3) Token cost surge with autoregressive mode switch
   - Profile: simulated conversation that flips to long-form generative mode 1 in 10 sessions.
   - Metric to watch: tokens per session, spike > 3x baseline -> check batching config and caching efficacy.

4) Regional capacity failover and graceful degradation
   - Profile: region A goes 40% degraded, traffic routed to region B.
   - Verify: routing policy honors cost-optimized fallback, and customer tiering kept for enterprise routes.

5) A/B leakage and contamination simulation
   - Profile: cohort assignment drift (5% of A users misrouted to B).
   - Detect: statistical test for contamination, cohort-level telemetry delta.

Simulation mechanics (how we run):
- Environments: staging-sim (no real keys), preprod (mirrors infra but isolated), lab-run (single-node containerized).
- Tools: traffic-synth v2, synthetic-user-sequences (csv), chaos-injector (latency/jitter/failures).
- Data seeding: use obfuscated recorded traces (last 30 days) + synthetic edge cases (malformed prompts, high-token loops).
- Run cadence: quick smoke (30m), standard sim (3–6h), full-day soak (24h) for high-risk launches.

Signal map and owners:
- Latency: infra/serving-runtime (primary), SRE (secondary)
- Error rate / 5xx: serving-runtime (primary), release-engineering (secondary)
- Model quality (accept rate, rerank delta): applied-ml (primary), product-owner (secondary)
- Cost (tokens/session, GPU utilization): finance-and-legal? (watch), infra (primary)
- Safety flags / toxic outputs: trust-and-safety (primary), product (secondary)

Decision heuristics (simulated thresholds):
- Green -> continue: p95 latency within 1.5x baseline, no sustained quality delta, error rate < 0.5% above baseline.
- Pause -> investigation window: any single signal crossing (p95 > 2x baseline OR quality delta > 5% OR error spike sustained > 5m). Traffic held at current exposure while oncall triages for up to 30m.
- Rollback -> automated rollback to previous model/route when two or more signal families cross critical thresholds for > 10m (examples: p99 latency > 3x baseline AND error rate > 2% above baseline).
- Canary abort -> immediate reversion when safety flag rate increases > 200% relative to baseline or any verified high-severity safety hit reported.

Orchestration choreography (sim runbook excerpt):
1) Prep: confirm sim dataset, tag model version, reserve test infra (owners: release-eng + infra).
2) Dry-run: local run for 6–10 minutes to validate configs (owner: applied-ml).
3) Lab smoke: synthetic traffic at 10% of target cohort for 30 minutes. Capture telemetry snapshots.
4) Standard sim: ramp to 100% of planned cohort traffic for 3 hours. Run chaos-injector scenarios at defined windows.
5) Observation: product + applied-ml perform manual quality review at 60/120/180 minutes.
6) Decision: follow Decision heuristics above. Document decisions in the sim run log.
7) Postmortem: owners collate logs and produce a 1-page sim outcome summary for the rollout ticket.

Practical checklist for teams before live canary (derived from sim runs):
- Infra: capacity reservation confirmed, autoscale thresholds set, emergency-shed endpoint configured.
- Release: canary policy defined (cohort sizes, ramp schedule, rollback policy, observation windows).
- Product: telemetry dashboards verified and shared, human-review allocation scheduled, communication plan drafted.
- Trust & Safety: safety hook enabled, human-review path tested with seeded hits.
- SRE: oncall roster assigned, pager rules validated, escalation contacts listed.
- Finance: cost-guard set (soft cap alert + hard cap kill switch notified).

Open questions and trade-offs (working):
- How aggressive should batch sizing be during canary vs full rollout? Sim shows larger batches reduce cost but amplify tail latency under mixed load. Trade: unit cost vs p99 risk.
- Should we allow automated rollback to a lower-quality but cheaper model variant to preserve latency? Cost-saving vs UX/regression risk.
- What minimum synthetic coverage is acceptable for safety hooks? Tension between recall of safety detectors and false positives in sim.

Simulation artifacts we should capture and attach to the rollout ticket:
- Telemetry export (CSV): latency histograms, error logs, token counts per session.
- Synthetic traffic definition (yaml) and seed corpus.
- Chaos injection timeline and parameters.
- Manual review notes with sampled prompts and model outputs.
- Short summary: decisions made and rationale (1 page).

Mini incident playbook (for sim-driven rehearsal):
- Trigger: p99 > 5x baseline OR verified safety incident flagged by human review.
- Immediate action (0–5m): pause any further ramp, notify rollback authority, collect core dumps.
- Triage (5–30m): infra checks (GPU, network), model variant sanity checks, check routing/fallbacks. Product to start user-impact assessment.
- Remediation (30m–3h): rollback if unresolved OR apply emergency config (reduce batch size, enable more aggressive caching) and monitor.
- Communication: short incident artefact posted to rollout ticket, + 1-line slack update to stakeholders.

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Add script to automatically compare sim telemetry to historical preprod baselines. (owner: Marco)
- Add a teardown sanity check that validates no leftover test-model endpoints remain after sim (owner: DevOps).
- Run a scheduled sim next quarter to validate newer quantized variants (owner: applied-ml).
- Flesh out the contamination-detection statistical test and include sample notebook (owner: Sofia).

Appendix: quick commands and references
- Quick sim run (dev-machine): traffic-synth --profile lab-long-short --duration 180m --tag sim-2025-01
- Chaos injections: chaos-injector --latency 200,500 --error-rate 0.01 --at 45m --duration 10m
- Collecting telemetry: telemetry-export --range last-3h --prefix sim-2025-01 --out ./artifacts

Concluding notes:
This doc is intentionally pragmatic and toggles between prescriptive thresholds and experiment-driven knobs. Use the sim runs to build trust across teams: the goal is not to eliminate all risk, but to make failure modes visible and playbooks executable before real users see them.

If you iterate on this, please append sim-run timestamps and short summaries so the rollout history tells a clear story.
